_strings.@@2a8d88698fb3: Treaty conformity — AL does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by AL. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Alabama does NOT start the return from federal adjusted gross income. Both the resident Form 40 and the nonresident Form 40NR build Alabama income from their own line items computed under Alabama law (2024 Form 40 line 5b wages/salaries/tips from Schedule W-2 line 18 column I plus column J — line 5a, column A, is Alabama income tax withheld from Schedule W-2 line 18 column G — line 6 interest and dividends, line 7 other income; Form 40NR equivalents), not by importing a federal AGI figure. Because the federal-AGI-conformity flow-through does not exist here, a treaty exclusion that is already netted out of federal AGI does NOT automatically carry to the Alabama return. The 2024 Form 40NR booklet (24f40nrbk.pdf, Other Income/Foreign Income Exclusion) is explicit on the only foreign-income mechanism it recognizes: 'All foreign income must be reported on your return, in order to receive any foreign income exclusion,' and that exclusion is the IRC sec. 911 foreign EARNED income exclusion, claimed as a negative entry on line 8 Other Income with federal Form 2555 attached. There is NO Alabama line, schedule, or instruction that recognizes or excludes income exempt under a U.S. income-TAX TREATY. Given (a) the separate Alabama income build-up rather than a federal-AGI start, and (b) the affirmative 'report all foreign income' rule with only a sec. 911-style exclusion path, conformity to federal treaty exemptions is NOT established on any .gov page. Per conservative handling this is set false and flagged. See unverified/notes.
_strings.@@4518b9b4a6d4: Rural Physician Credit — Licensed physicians who practice and reside in a small or rural Alabama community of fewer than 25,000 residents, with admission privileges to a 'small or rural hospital' that has an emergency room (acute care hospital with fewer than 105 beds, located more than 20 miles from another acute care facility, or receiving Medicare rural reimbursement). Does not apply to physicians who met the requirements on/before May 5, 1993, nor to a physician who previously practiced in such a community unless they return after practicing in a large/urban community for at least three years.
_strings.@@4bbbf6b75e22: Credit for Taxes Paid to Another State — Legal residents of Alabama filing Form 40 who have income from sources outside Alabama that is taxed by BOTH Alabama and another U.S. state or territory in the same tax year. (Part-year residents only if the AL and other-state returns cover the same periods. No credit when the out-of-state income is totally offset by a corresponding deduction. Schedule CR must be completed with a copy of the other state's return attached — or W-2Gs if the taxing state does not allow a return to be filed for gambling winnings.)

Subtract line 15 from line 10.'); booklet Line 17 Figuring Your Tax (p.10): 'You must figure your tax from the Tax Tables unless you are claiming a carryover or carryback Net Operating Loss from another year.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 UNCHANGED: the 2024 booklet's What's New page lists only credit changes (Volunteer First Responder Mileage credit, Preceptor Tax Incentive, refund check-offs, MAT pre-approval) — the 2%/4%/5% dual schedules, sliding standard deduction chart, $1,500/$3,000 personal exemptions, income-tiered dependent exemption, and the over-$100,000 worksheet constants were each re-verified from the 2024 prints, not assumed. Base guidance: Supply 2024 Alabama Form 40, page 1, line 16 'Taxable income. Subtract line 15 from line 10.' Alabama does NOT start from federal AGI: line 10 Alabama adjusted gross income is built from Alabama line items (line 8 total income = line 5b wages + line 6 interest/dividends + line 7 other income, minus line 9 adjustments), and line 15 total deductions = line 11 (itemized OR sliding standard deduction) + line 12 (FEDERAL income tax deduction, from the Federal Income Tax Deduction Worksheet) + line 13 (personal exemption $1,500/$3,000) + line 14 (income-dependent dependent exemption). All of those subtractions must already be taken on the form before line 16 — this op subtracts nothing further. Tax-table mandate: the 2024 Form 40 booklet (Line 17 instructions, p.10) states 'You must figure your tax from the Tax Tables unless you are claiming a carryover or carryback Net Operating Loss from another year.' The Tax Table (booklet pp. 25-30) covers taxable income under $100,000 in $100-wide bands priced at the band midpoint, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands (booklet example: MFJ $23,360 -> table $1,088 vs bracket math $1,088.00 exact at the midpoint); the filed form must use the table. Over $100,000: the 2024 booklet's worksheet (p. 30) computes tax as $4,958.00 (Single/MFS/Head of Family) or $4,918.00 (MFJ) plus 5% of taxable income over $100,000. Those printed constants are each $2 LESS than the exact cumulative bracket sums ($4,960 / $4,920) because they carry forward the last tax-table row's midpoint value (the $99,900-$100,000 row prints $4,958/$4,918); above $100,000 the tax the form produces is therefore $2 lower than this op's pure bracket math. FEDERAL income tax deduction quirk: Alabama allows a base deduction for federal income tax liability (Form 40 line 12; Federal Income Tax Deduction Worksheet, booklet p. 31: 2024 Form 1040/1040-SR/1040-NR line 22 plus Form 8960 line 17 net investment income tax, minus refundable EIC, Additional Child Tax Credit, American Opportunity Credit, and Form 2439 credits). It is already inside the line 16 base this op consumes — do not re-subtract it. standard_deduction is NOT shipped because Alabama's standard deduction slides with Alabama AGI (2024 booklet p. 9 chart, amounts unchanged from 2023): MFJ $8,500 (AL AGI $0-$25,999) phasing down to $5,000 at $35,500 and above; MFS $4,250 ($0-$12,999) down to $2,500 at $17,750 and above; Head of Family $5,200 ($0-$25,999) down to $2,500 at $35,500 and above; Single $3,000 ($0-$25,999) down to $2,500 at $35,500 and above. Take it from the chart on Form 40 line 11; it is already inside line 16. Personal exemption (Form 40 line 13) is $1,500 (Single or Married Filing Separately) / $3,000 (Married Filing Jointly or Head of Family), printed on the 2024 Form 40 filing-status boxes 1-4. It is a base reduction, but it is already inside the line 16 base this op consumes, so it is NOT shipped as an engine exemption. Dependent exemption (Form 40 line 14) is income-dependent and NOT shipped: $1,000 per dependent when Alabama AGI (line 10) is $0-$50,000; $500 when $50,001-$100,000; $300 when over $100,000 (2024 booklet p. 8 chart, unchanged). It is already inside line 16 — claim it on the form, not through this op. One rate schedule covers Single, Married Filing Separately, and Head of Family (2% on the first $500, 4% on the next $2,500, 5% over $3,000); Married Filing Jointly has its own schedule (2% on the first $1,000, 4% on the next $5,000, 5% over $6,000). Alabama has no qualifying-surviving-spouse filing status (Form 40 boxes are Single / Married filing joint / Married filing separate / Head of Family, and the booklet's Head-of-Family definition requires the individual 'is not a surviving spouse'). The engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping does not correspond to an Alabama status — a filer widowed before 2024 files Single or Head of Family in Alabama, so do not rely on the MFJ schedule for a federal QSS filer. The 2%/4%/5% schedule text is printed on the ADOR FAQ 'What is Alabama's Individual Income Tax Rate?' (https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faqs/what-is-alabamas-individual-income-tax-rate/) and was verified numerically against the 2024 booklet's Tax Table rows (e.g. $16,000-$16,100 -> $763 single / $723 MFJ; $4,100-$4,200 -> $168 / $146) and the over-$100,000 worksheet.
